what: Truist Financial is a large US regional bank formed by the merger of BB&T and SunTrust. It serves households and businesses across the southeastern United States and runs commercial banking and an investment bank.
customers: Consumers, small businesses and corporate clients, mainly in the Southeast and mid-Atlantic.
money: deposits, mortgages, car loans and credit cards
commercial lending, investment banking and treasury services
moat: Branch density and deposit share in fast-growing southeastern markets, which provides cheap, stable funding.
risks: Commercial property loans are a watched area for all regional banks
Deposit costs rise when customers move money to higher-yielding accounts
The BB&T and SunTrust integration consumed years of management attention
Regional bank regulation is being tightened
opportunities: Selling its insurance brokerage raised a large amount of capital for buybacks
Population and business growth in the Southeast is above the national average
A dividend yield above 4% while the balance sheet is repositioned
watch: Net interest margin and credit quality in commercial property lending.
